title: Reinstatement Guidelines: Computing the Term Life Insurance Reinstatement Amount
content:
**Term Life Insurance — reinstatement amount.** The reinstatement amount that reinstates a lapsed policy under an approved reinstatement application is the back premium plus the reinstatement interest plus the repeat reinstatement charge, rounded to the cent.

| Element | Definition |
|---|---|
| Back premium | the total of every billed installment on the ledger, less every remittance applied, plus every payment returned unpaid by the bank |
| Lapse gap | the number of calendar days from the lapse date on record to the date the approved reinstatement application was signed |
| Reinstatement interest rate | the product's reinstatement interest rate |
| Long-standing policy concession | nothing |
| Relationship share of the interest | the whole interest |
| Interest days | the calendar days from the paid-to date at lapse (the paid-to date on record) to today |
| Reinstatement interest | the back premium times the reinstatement interest rate less the long-standing policy concession, times the relationship share, times the interest days over 365 — simple, and rounded to the cent once on the total |
| Repeat reinstatement charge | nothing |

The interest is computed once on the whole back premium, not installment by installment, and is rounded only once.

### Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

Back premium 630.00 (three quarterly installments of 210.00 billed and unpaid); reinstatement interest rate 0.06; paid-to date at lapse 1 January 2026; today 15 May 2026, which is 134 calendar days later.

- Reinstatement interest: 630.00 times 0.06 times 134 over 365, which is 13.877…, rounded to 13.88.
- Reinstatement amount: 630.00 plus 13.88 plus nothing, which is 643.88.
